title: How former Penn State players are performing in NFL training camp
author: Andrew Deal | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State just reported to fall camp on Tuesday, and a new group of former Penn Staters have begun their first training camp in the NFL. Others are entering yet another year of camp before the start of the season.

Here’s training camp news and standouts from former Nittany Lions.

Drew Allar

Drew Allar made headlines during rookie minicamp in the spring when it was made known that new Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy would be starting with Allar from scratch.

McCarthy has seemingly taken Allar under his wing, having been seen coaching him one-on-one, showing that there’s belief Allar could become a starter at some point in his career.

That’s been evident in the early parts of Steelers training camp, as Allar has made impressive passes and plays day in and day out. The consistency is the biggest factor for Allar, who’s already showed off his cannon of an arm. He’s also shown he can place the ball well as he continues improving his footwork.

While Allar likely won’t see any playing time in the regular season, barring injury from Aaron Rodgers, he’s expected to get significant minutes in the preseason as the backup battle continues with Will Howard.

Nick Singleton

Another rookie, Nick Singleton was seen Tuesday getting a handoff from Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward. While that on the surface doesn’t seem meaningful, it shows Singleton is receiving first-team reps.

The Titans used a fifth-round pick on Singleton in the 2026 NFL Draft, and with one of the worst rushing attacks in the NFL last year, the former Penn State standout could add a spark to the run game.

Singleton will be in battle with Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears for playing time, but if the rookie shows the burst that he showed across his career at Penn State, he could quickly move ahead of them.

Joey Porter Jr.

Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. isn’t exactly holding out while he works to get a contract extension with the Steelers, as he’s been present at training camp while also dealing with a back injury.

Porter has turned himself into a bonafide top cornerback in the league, and with recent contract extensions from other cornerbacks in his draft class, he could earn big money from the Steelers.

Pittsburgh hasn’t made any reported progress on an extension with the former Penn Stater, but hold-ins have been a common practice among Steeler players looking for an extension, and all have earned them in prior years.

Nittany Lions on new teams

Multiple former Nittany Lions are making their training camp debut on new rosters ahead of the 2026 season. Edge rusher Odafe Oweh, safety Jaquan Brisker and wide receiver Jahan Dotson are among the names donning new jerseys.

Oweh has opened eyes at training camp with the Washington Commanders after signing a four-year, $100 million deal with the Commanders in March. His speed off the edge has caused immediate issues for Washington’s top offensive unit.

Brisker returned to his home city of Pittsburgh to man the backline of the Steelers’ defense. With many questions in the safety room, Brisker has provided consistent play in practice and is set to be one of the starters, potentially alongside Jalen Ramsey.

Dotson is on his third team, now with the Atlanta Falcons, and has quickly grown a connection with quarterback Michael Penix Jr. In a receiving core that features Drake London and Kyle Pitts, Dotson is likely to have a lot of one-on-one opportunities to make an impact on the Falcons.

Tight ends

Penn State has inserted its name in the “Tight End U” conversation, and the tight ends are continuing to show why in training camp.

Tyler Warren is making spectacular catch after spectacular catch in Indianapolis. Warren finished fifth in receiving yards with 817 among tight ends in his rookie year despite his usage significantly dropping when Daniel Jones went down with an injury. Warren could be in for another big year with his quarterback back to full health ahead of the season.

Pat Freiermuth once again looks to be one of Rodgers’ favorite targets, and with a revamped offense, the former Nittany Lion could be in for a big year. In offenses with Rodgers and McCarthy, the tight end was a significant part of the gameplan, and Freiermuth’s ability to work the middle of the field has already shown in training camp.

Brenton Strange is entering training camp with a new contract. The tight end earned a three-year, $48 million deal after a strong 2025 campaign and became one of Trevor Lawrence’s most reliable targets. Theo Johnson, on the other hand, has struggled to hold onto the ball in training camp in a year where he could see less time with the addition of Isaiah Likely on the New York Giants.

title: Way-too-early season predictions for Penn State women’s basketball
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
It’s a new era of Penn State women’s basketball, with Tanisha Wright leading the charge since being hired in March.

Along the way, she’s recruited a team of nine athletes, which was much needed after every player hit the transfer portal from the year before.

With the new start and new team comes a lot of unanswered questions on how the team will compete this year. Who will be the leading scorers and go-to players? Will this team have what it takes to compete in the Big Ten?

Here are some way-too-early predictions for the Lady Lions’ 2026-27 campaign, which is now less than 100 days away.

Kamrah Banks will be top-3 team scorer

Despite being a freshman, Kamrah Banks has one of the highest ceilings for anyone on the team this year.

The 4-star guard graduated from Crispus Attucks High School in Indianapolis, where she left her mark with several school records. Among them was the all-time leading scorer and most points in a single game — a record previously held by NBA Hall of Famer Oscar Robertson.

While freshmen haven’t seen astronomical minutes in recent years for the Lady Lions, this year’s squad is much different. No one is as dominant as Gracie Merkle or Kiyomi McMiller and many spots in the starting lineup are likely up for grabs.

I believe Banks has the capability to be a starter early on. She may not get the nod in the first game due to her lack of collegiate experience, but the buzz surrounding her, coupled with whatever she can do off the bench, should earn her a starting role before the conference slate.

Even off the bench, I’d expect her to be one of the more dominant scorers on Penn State. She averaged 20.4 points per game her senior year and 26.4 points her junior year and has proven to be a capable offensive weapon.

Lady Lions will lose at least 1 ‘should-win’ games

Penn State has nine players on its roster who’ve never played together. No matter the number of summer workouts and fall practices, you can’t recreate in-game scenarios until it’s gametime.

The Lady Lions’ nonconference schedule hasn’t been released yet, but often opens with several Group of Six programs, including Bucknell, Cincinnati and Coppin State last season.

While these should result in wins for the Lady Lions, or any Big Ten team for that matter, the lack of chemistry could create issues early in the season.

I don’t expect the blue and white to come out of the nonconference stretch with a losing record, but I wouldn’t be surprised if it has a few losses to its name, even against an opponent it should beat.

Penn State will run 4 guard offense

With just nine players on its roster, Penn State doesn’t have much depth anywhere. However, the Lady Lions only have three forwards, giving very little relief to whoever makes the starting lineup.

Petra Božan and Cristen Carter are both experienced post players who will likely battle it out for a starting role, with the other coming off the bench with a large role. Freshman Irene García offers another player at forward, but was both a late addition to the team and someone with limited experience — likely giving her a very minimal role.

Instead, Penn State’s six guards offer many years of collegiate experience and will likely take up a large part of the starting five.

Between junior Devyn Quigley and graduate student Enjulina Gonzalez, the Lady Lions have experience in the guard room. With sophomores Ava Black and Skylar Durley, and freshmen Banks and Ashlee Brown, there’s enough depth to run a four guard, one forward lineup.

title: 6 viral recipes to try before summer ends
author: Colleen Cratty | For The Collegian
description:
August is upon us, meaning there’s only a few weeks left to enjoy the warm weather. It’s the perfect time to try out some new recipes and soak in those summer vibes.

Whether you’re hosting a barbecue, packing a beach picnic or just looking for a fun meal to make at home, here are six viral recipes to try.

Grillo’s Pickle Dip

This recipe is sure to indulge those with a savory tooth, with its creamy and crunchy mixture of pickles and cream cheese.

With the addition of ranch powder seasoning and crumbled bacon, this dip is a great appetizer paired with some plain potato chips or crackers.

If you’re into spicy food, you can use Grillo’s hot spears and add jalapeños for an extra kick.

This recipe is easy to make, it just requires chopping pickles into a bowl to mix them with some other ingredients. Grillo’s even recommends serving it in the pickle container, so it's perfect for those who like to reuse or college students on a budget. It also travels well, making it a great snack to bring to a cookout!

Trader Joe’s sandwich

This viral recipe is a classic for a lover of Trader Joe’s, a trip to the beach or a quick lunch between summer jobs.

This sandwich uses sun-dried tomato focaccia, the perfect way to inject summer energy into a simple sandwich. The sandwich has turkey, greens, tomatoes, mayonnaise and pesto, creating a fresh and foolproof summer sandwich. You could also remove the turkey for a vegetarian twist.

However you choose to make it, it’s a great choice for a sunny day.

Crispy pasta salad

Pasta salad is a staple when it comes to summer activities, like a picnic or barbecue. But this one puts a special spin on the classic!

Instead of just boiling the pasta, this recipe encourages you to air fry it after, with olive oil and seasoning to create a nice crunch. The crispy pasta is also paired with fresh produce like romaine, cherry tomatoes, red onion and cucumber, as well as feta cheese. The feta brings a tangy flavor, and it can easily be substituted with a vegan version for those avoiding dairy.

Baked feta pasta

This recipe has done numbers on social media and is often called the “TikTok pasta.”

It's super easy to make when you just want to throw something in the oven. All you have to do is put some chopped garlic, a chopped shallot, a block of feta cheese and some grape tomatoes in a casserole dish and bake it. Boil some bowtie pasta, mix up the sauce and now you’ve got a delicious summer pasta.

Most recipes recommend adding in some crushed red pepper flakes for a nice kick to balance out the tangy sauce.

Crunchy cucumber salad

This cucumber salad is a tasty and easy snack for the beach or a perfect side dish for a barbecue.

For the salad, chop up some cucumber and toss it in a dressing. You could use a pre-made italian dressing, make one with olive oil and red wine vinegar or add some sesame oil, ginger and chili crisp for an Asian-inspired dressing.

Some people also like to add sliced onions, avocado or sesame seeds for a variety in texture. Since it only takes a few minutes to prepare, it’s an easy recipe to throw together whenever you need a refreshing snack or side dish.

Fluffy seagull iced latte

This is a great summer drink option, inspired by a viral latte made by the Cape Cod coffee shop, Lighthouse Keepers.

Make a latte with your favorite espresso and choice of milk in a glass lined with marshmallow fluff and peanut butter, and you’ve got a Fluffy Seagull. You can also make a marshmallow cold foam with fluff, heavy cream and milk to top off the drink.

This latte is easy to make and a delicious way to get in some much-needed caffeine in the morning.

title: Off the record | Sociable Sarah
author: Miss Behave I The Daily Collegian
description:
Editor’s Note: Off the record is a weekly column written by a fourth-year Collegian staffer under an alias. It aims to promote a space for honest conversations about love, sex and relationships. Those interested in sharing their experiences or submitting a topic can do so through this anonymous form.

Dear Sarah,

Senior year is filled with so many final moments. Final first day of school. Final football game. Final late night with your girlfriends.

While I’m sure you recognize that male validation shouldn’t make or break your big senior year, it shouldn’t be a driving force in your life right now. Don’t think your year is a bust if you don’t leave with a boyfriend. You would be crushed if you spent the year pining for someone who couldn’t care less if you lived or died, or better yet, pursued someone who “isn’t ready” for anything.

Luckily for you, I have the perfect solution for all this yearning. Instead of yearning for a rom-com-type love, pour all that love into the people who have been there for you through everything — your girlfriends. They’re there for you when romantic love fails; they pick up all the pieces and then force you to eat your weight in ice cream.

There’s never going to be another time in your life when all your friends are a walk away, or you’re staying up until 3 a.m. laughing about all the dumb decisions you’ve made the day prior.

The relationships you should be preserving are the ones you already have, rather than withering away in a nonstop search for something more. I promise boyfriends aren’t as fulfilling as they may sound. College is where you find your bridesmaids, not your husband!

I understand people can balance a romantic partner and their friends seamlessly, but why take the chance and ruin a good thing? It’s a tale as old as time: girl has amazing friends, girl meets boyfriend, girl spends a lot of time with said boy, girl loses friends because they’re fed up with her constantly ditching them. Why let this be you when you can stay on that first chapter, the girl who has amazing friends?

In your final year, you have a lot on your plate: internships, jobs, graduation, and you don’t need a man who can’t be bothered added to the mix. Your girlfriends are the perfect combination of low stakes and low commitment. They get that some days you're going to respond to their message five hours later, and sometimes you’re not in the mood to bar crawl on a random Wednesday night. They know you love them and don’t have to prove it every minute of every day for it to be true.

You have your whole life to date crappy men, but you won’t always have your girlfriends there to debrief Sunday morning over an iced latte and Irving’s bagel. I’m drooling just thinking about it.

The truth is that I’ve been on dates, counting down the minutes until I could go back home and see my friends. The men were fine, but there’s something so special about my girls. I would be out with him, wishing I were with them.

One time, I canceled on him because my girls were getting triple dippers from Chili's in Altoona. I’m a girl with amazing friends and priorities.

Your senior year isn’t the time to get your heart broken. It’ll throw off the vibes for a while, and you’ll be kicking yourself that you let a loser ruin your plans.

We’ve all heard the stories about the couples who meet in college, get married, blah blah blah. Maybe your senior year feels like a last-ditch effort to secure that picture-perfect fairytale ending, but college isn’t the only place where you’ll meet a relationship-worthy partner.

You should be having fun, drinking (if you're of age, of course), partying and ever so occasionally studying.

I’m kidding. Please make sure you graduate.

I want you to have the best senior year imaginable, boyfriend or not. But let’s be real — preferably not. I have a strong feeling that when you’re crossing the stage, you’ll be thankful you spent time with your friends instead of the guy who claims he can’t do long-distance.

Until next time,

Miss Behave

title: On ‘one little, tiny rock,’ astronomers have split from astrology
author: Allison Shanley | For The Collegian
description:
It’s become an increasingly common practice to ask for someone’s zodiac sign, whether it be in search of compatibility or a result of mere curiosity. It’s displayed on dating profiles, inked on the pages of newspapers, sold as keychains at gift shops.

Before these modern trends, astrology had a reputable place in scholarly traditions, with astronomy and astrology originally seen as two sides of the same coin. But throughout astronomy’s scientific revolution, research resulted in crossroads between astrologers and astronomers, and the two concepts drifted apart.

Astrology is the belief that the position of celestial bodies influences people’s lives. Astronomy is the scientific study of these bodies; it’s mathematics, using systems of calculations to predict where planets have been and where they will be, Jason Wright, a professor of astronomy and astrophysics, said.

“Over the decades, you see the planets move through all of the constellations of the zodiac,” Wright said.

Those patterns, tracked over centuries, became the basis for astrology. Horoscopes, Wright said, were based on the motions of the planets.

Many have continued using interpretations of celestial cycles based on solar calendars as a tool for insight on one’s personal life, but it used to be less inclusionary.

“Early astronomers like (Johannes) Kepler were given wages to be an astronomer, and to have the patronage of wealthy people and royalty by astrology,” Wright said.

Astrology has since evolved from being a service exclusively for the wealthy, largely due to a newspaper column publication by astrologer R.H Naylor in the 1930s. Today, horoscopes have remained a popular fixture of newspapers.

As such, people popularly analyze their birth charts, mapping out where the planets were at the time they were born. The horoscope hashtag on TikTok has approximately 2.1 million posts; on Instagram, 7.7 million.

A more practical use of astronomy was the creation of the calendar. Each zodiac season, a new constellation appears behind it, and each cycle makes up the 12 seasons of the zodiac.

But Kevin Luhman, a professor of astronomy and astrophysics, said axial precession creates inconsistencies between earth's calendar and the ecliptic path on which the sun is located.

Luhman said a person’s zodiac sign traditionally reflects which constellation the sun appeared in front of at the time of their birth. For example, he said, the sun was in front of the constellation of Sagittarius for a person born a Sagittarius.

This system was set up by the Babylonians in 500 B.C.E. But because of the way Earth’s axis has since shifted, the sun is no longer in front of the zodiac traditionally assigned to it.

“Today, if you're born at that time of year, the sun is not in front of the Sagittarius,” Luhman said. “By studying the history of astronomy, one can learn a lot about the origin of astrology as well.”

Nahks Tr'Ehnl, an instructional technology specialist within the department of astronomy and astrophysics, said with modern astronomical understanding, astrology has been a practice “left behind in astronomy.”

He said that over thousands of years, scientists have refined instruments to aid physics and mathematical systems so each generation understands things in a way nobody has before.

“Sometimes folks will have the belief, before taking an astronomy course, that Earth is the center of the universe,” Tr'Ehnl said. “Once you've taken the astronomy course, you know the Earth is actually just this one little, tiny rock orbiting a pretty ordinary star somewhere in the galaxy.”

He said the “you're-really-not-special-at-all” feeling that arises from such a realization is a common one. The manifestation of mythical, magical characteristics in astrology, he said, can be accredited to the human perspective of being fascinated with the cosmos.

“Humans are special in the sense that we're the first living creatures — that we know about — that understands the right to choose what they want to believe,” Tr'Ehnl said.

title: Penn State women's volleyball releases 2026 promotional schedule
author: Rafael Rivera | For the Collegian
description:
On Wednesday, Penn State women’s volleyball released its promotional schedule for the 2026 season.

Many annual events will be returning, highlighted by Penn State hosting its Dig Pink event on Oct. 3 against Iowa, and a Halloween White Out game on Oct. 31 against Purdue.

September is set to be big for Penn State, as it will host Ohio on Sept. 12 in the second annual Team Ream match. The match was made to honor the legacy of former Penn State football player Brandon Ream. Team Ream is an organization that looks to raise awareness and funding for the fight against cancer.

Three days later, on Sept. 15, the blue and white will host Villanova for a Keep It In PA night. On Sept. 18, they will play USF with a Beach Bash theme and then will round out the busy week with a Pre Match Block Party against Tennessee on Sept. 20.

On Oct. 9th Penn State will team up with the V Foundation to host the annual THON game against Northwestern. The foundation has funded over $458 million dollars for cancer research, and coach Katie Schumacher-Cawley won the Jimmy V award for perseverance at the ESPYs after winning a national championship while undergoing treatment for breast cancer.

To round out the Promotional schedule, Penn State will honor military service members during Military Appreciation night on Oct. 29.

title: Report: Former Penn State player Jalen Pickett agrees to two-way deal with Los Angeles Clippers
author: Will Horstman | The Daily Collegian
description:
After entering NBA free agency just over a month ago, guard Jalen Pickett has found his next team.

Pickett and the Los Angeles Clippers have agreed to a two-way deal, according to Michael Scotto of Hoops Hype. The contract will allow Pickett to split time between the Clippers and their G League affiliate, the San Diego Clippers.

Pickett spent the past three seasons with the Denver Nuggets, who declined his team option earlier this summer, making him an unrestricted free agent. Pickett played in 50 games during the 2025-26 season, averaging 5.2 points per game.

This past season included a career-high night for Pickett, who scored 29 points during a win over the Philadelphia 76ers in January. Pickett started 18 games last season as he was a key depth piece when the Nuggets were facing injuries in their usual starting lineup.

Pickett was selected with the 32nd overall pick in the second round of the 2023 NBA draft by the Indiana Pacers, who traded his draft rights to Denver. Pickett played in 126 games with the Nuggets, averaging 4.0 points, 1.6 rebounds and 1.9 assists per game.

Prior to his NBA career, Pickett became a second-team All-American with Penn State in 2022-23, leading the Nittany Lions to the second round of the NCAA Tournament. He averaged 17.7 points, 7.4 rebounds and 6.6 assists per game during his memorable campaign.

Now, as Pickett starts the next step in his NBA journey, he'll get to be teammates with former Penn State player Yanic Konan Niederhauser on the Clippers.

title: Former Fairfield outfielder TJ Schmalzle signs with Penn State Baseball
author: Rafael Rivera | For the Collegian
description:
Penn State has added another bat to its transfer portal class.

Senior outfielder TJ Schmalzle has officially signed with Penn State baseball, the team announced Wednesday.

Schmalzle played three seasons at Fairfield College, batting .269 while racking up 127 hits, 19 home runs and 49 stolen bases. In his freshman season in 2023, Schmalzle did not play due to injury; but he stayed on the field for the following three seasons, playing in 134 games..

The Hawley, Pennsylvania native had a great 2026 season, hitting 285. and earning All-MAAC second team honors while also being one of 10 D1 players with 11+ home runs and 25+ steals in 2026.

Schmalzle's speed and with power will make him one of Penn State's key offseason additions, as he could be set to make an immediate impact.

title: Former Richmond reliever Dom Ruggerio signs with Penn State baseball
author: Rafael Rivera | For the Collegian
description:
Penn State has made another pitching move in the transfer portal, as the team announced the signing of former University of Richmond standout Dom Ruggerio on Wednesday.

Ruggiero is a 6-foot-2 left handed relief pitcher from Royersford, PA, where he attended Spring-Ford Area High School. He'll be a sophomore in his first year at Penn State.

In his first collegiate season at Richmond University Ruggerio posted a 3.76 ERA in 26.1 innings of work, and ended his season with 28 strikeouts and 15 walks.

Ruggiero will add more proven collegiate experience to Penn State's bullpen for 2027 and beyond.

title: Penn State baseball signs Michigan State transfer infielder Ryan McKay
author: Dominic Megats I The Daily Collegian
description:
An eventful day for coach Gambino and his staff continued on Tuesday.

Former infielder from Michigan State Ryan McKay signed with Penn State, the team announced on X.

The Clarkston, Michigan, native abandons his hometown and makes his way to Happy Valley after starting in 161 games for the Spartans. Throughout those games, McKay totaled 168 hits, 84 RBI and 21 steals. Additionally, he currently owns a career .275 batting average.

The rising senior was named to Second-Team All-Big Ten after an impressive sophomore campaign in which he posted a .319 batting average in 54 games.

With primary second baseman Jayden Davis leaving the team, McKay should have a clear path to filling that role for the Nittany Lions.

title: Penn State TEs Benjamin Brahmer, Gabe Burkle land on John Mackey Award watch list
author: Andrew Deal | The Daily Collegian
description:
Two more Nittany Lions have landed on an award watch list.

Tight ends Benjamin Brahmer and Gabe Burkle have been named to the John Mackey Award watch list, recognizing the top tight end in the country.

Brahmer and Burkle were both named to the list last year at Iowa State, with Brahmer finishing as a semifinalist. The duo has a chance to add their names to a recent list of Penn State tight end greats, including Tyler Warren, who won the award in 2024.

Brahmer is coming off a year where he caught 37 passes for 446 yards and six touchdowns, all career highs. Brahmer is nearing the 1,000 receiving-yard mark in his career with 977 yards right now.

Burkle played alongside Brahmer last year, earning 302 yards on 26 receptions before tearing his ACL in November. With the return of Andrew Rappleyea and Brahmer potentially in front of him, it's unknown how much production Burkle will have this year.

It's the sixth straight season with at least one Penn State tight end earning a spot on the Mackey Award watch list, as Brahmer and Burkle join Khalil Dinkins, Warren, Theo Johnson and Brenton Strange as previous members on the list, all in the 2020s.

description:
Penn State will have a Stripe Out for Matt Campbell's debut as head coach.

The Nittany Lions announced Wednesday that their home opener against Marshall in Week 1 will be a Stripe Out.

title: Preview | Penn State women’s soccer 2026 schedule full of rivalries, rematches
author: Mashiah Mitchell | For the Collegian
description:
The beginning of the fall semester brings the subsequent kickoff of the 2026 season for coach Erica Dambach’s Nittany Lions.

Dambach and her team have not seen a national championship since their one and only in 2015. They’ll likely be looking to work back to that level after a lackluster 2025 campaign that ended with their worst record under her leadership since 2010.

Despite the record, the Nittany Lions still returned to the NCAA tournament for the 32nd consecutive season, though it would be a short stint, with the squad losing in the second round to the University of Virginia.

This year’s 17-game schedule for the Nittany Lions is filled with conference contenders along with a few fresh opponents, including a first-time, never-before-seen nonconference meeting. Renewed rivalries, rematches and consistency is the name of the game for this year’s Nittany Lions.

The Nittany Lions will open their season on the road with back-to-back games against two teams that also made the NCAA tournament the previous season.

First, they’ll face the Notre Dame Fighting Irish on Aug. 16, a team that Dambach has never played and a team the Nittany Lions have not faced off against since 2006.

The Fighting Irish will return two of their three All-Americans in Izzy Engle and Annabelle Chukwu.

Then, they’ll take on the West Virginia Mountaineers on Aug. 20, who faced off against the Nittany Lions in their only away loss during the 2025 season.

Erica Dambach will also meet one of the greatest women’s coaches to ever grace the pitch, Nikki Izzo-Brown, who is entering her 30th season as the coach of the Mountaineers while looking to continue moving up the all-time wins list, now sitting at 425.

Then, the team will start a three-game homestand at Jeffrey Field in nonconference play, including the home opener against the Bucknell Bison on Aug. 27 and a first-time meeting with the Ivy League’s Brown University on Aug. 30.

The Nittany Lions will conclude non-conference play against a retooled Virginia Tech Hokies team that has seven incoming transfers on Sep. 3 before heading back on the road.

After that homestand is when the Nittany Lions’ season will begin picking up, with 12 straight Big Ten conference games and matchups against the defending Big Ten champions and runner-up.

The Big Ten slate starts in Columbus, Ohio, on Sep. 10 against a seasoned Ohio State Buckeyes team that has nearly ten returning seniors. It’s another rematch from last season for the Nittany Lions, one that resulted in a 2-0 win.

A familiar face will return to State College on Sep. 13, when the Nittany Lions play host to the Minnesota Golden Gophers. Former Penn State midfielder Keegan Schmeiser will make her first appearance in a different jersey since her 2024 transfer.

Another trip to the DMV is to follow on Sep. 18 against the Maryland Terrapins. The Nittany Lions will look to replicate their 4-0 win from last season and continue asserting dominance over a team still fairly new to the Big Ten compared to some of the other programs in the conference.

Then, it’s back home for a few weeks for the Nittany Lions. They’ll first play host to the Iowa Hawkeyes on Sep. 24, a team that just recently brought in new head coach Dean Ward after the departure of longtime boss Dave Dilanni.

Ward showed promise at Xavier University, leading the Musketeers to 31 wins and their first Big East Conference championship since 2019 in his short but meaningful two-year tenure. The matchup could be a defining game for the Nittany Lions.

After Iowa, they’ll take on two teams looking to get back to their former selves in the USC Trojans, who will take Jeffrey Field on Sep. 27 and the Purdue Boilermakers on Oct. 3.

After a disappointing season, USC added No. 1 freshman goalkeeper Josie Biehl to anchor their defense, which could possibly present problems for this year’s Nittany Lions.

Both teams finished in the bottom half of the Big Ten standings in 2025, unforeseen for a program like the Trojans that have been a consistent mainstay in the NCAA tournament.

The road then leads the Nittany Lions to Eugene, Oregon, on Oct. 8 to face the Oregon Ducks. Oregon finished dead last in the Big Ten just a year ago, winning only one conference game, interestingly enough against the eventual conference champion Washington Huskies.

Though their 3-10-5 record may say otherwise, this Oregon team presented hardship for the Nittany Lions last year in a 2-2 draw that was the difference maker in Penn State’s Big Ten ranking.

Quite possibly the biggest test of the season for the Nittany Lions will come on Oct. 11, when they travel to Seattle to face the Washington Huskies.

The Huskies are coming off their best season in program history, winning both the Big Ten regular season and tournament championships. They also reached the Elite Eight of the NCAA tournament for the first time since 2010.

Penn State will return home to face the Rutgers Scarlet Knights in a rivalry matchup on Oct. 17. The Scarlet Knights have not gotten the best of the Nittany Lions since the 2021 season in a 1-2 upset.

One more road trip will await the Nittany Lions after that, as they travel to the Mitten State to meet both Michigan State on Oct. 22 and Michigan on Oct. 25.

The season will close on Oct. 30 at Jeffrey Field against the Indiana Hoosiers.

Last season’s Hoosiers team managed a 1-2 upset against the Nittany Lions late in the year. With nine new freshmen additions along with eight seniors, Indiana could be primed for a resurgence in the Big Ten after a surprising bottom five finish.

title: 3 overlooked Penn State position groups heading into 2026 season
author: Andrew Mercer | The Daily Collegian
description:
Heading into the 2026 season, conversations about Penn State have been dominated by Rocco Becht’s return from injury, the running backs battling for reps and the continued success of one of the nation’s most prestigious linebacker rooms.

But there are other position groups flying under the radar for a range of reasons. Some positions don’t get talked about while others are overshadowed by the major headlines.

Some of those overlooked position groups are crucial to the overall success of the team, so here are three that aren’t being talked about enough.

Cornerback

Daryus Dixson, Audavion Collins and Zion Tracy at the nickel haven’t been discussed nearly as much as the rest of the defensive backfield.

With Tony Rojas and Jeremiah Cooper returning from injuries, a lot of focus is being put on how well they’ll perform. However, the cornerbacks can unlock the full potential of D’Anton Lynn’s scheme.

If the cornerbacks perform up to standard, the Nittany Lions can put more emphasis on the blitz without worrying about getting torched by the opponent’s deep ball. But if the cornerbacks fall short of expectations, more pressure is put on the linebackers and safeties to compensate for a lack of confidence after missed assignments.

On paper, this room has the experience required to improve from last season, with all three having returned to continue playing under Terry Smith. It becomes a matter of them smoothly operating under Lynn’s defensive scheme, in tandem with Smith’s current and prior coaching strategies.

IOL

The offensive tackles have received a lot of attention this offseason. One spot is held by two-year starter Anthony Donkoh, and the other position covering Becht’s blind side is up for grabs.

However, Penn State needs the interior linemen to perform at their best for the entire offensive system to come together.

Trevor Buhr, Brock Riker and Cooper Cousins are the current projected starters. Riker was the starting center at Texas State and was named a Second Team Freshman All-American by The Athletic, while Buhr and Cousins have experience from Iowa State and Penn State, respectively, and are projected to break out this season.

Cousins has been a consistent face on Penn State’s line for the past two years and is ready to make a big leap as a full-time starter. Buhr has already played under Mouser’s offensive scheme and Ryan Clanton’s coaching, offering first-hand experience blocking for Carson Hansen.

Riker impressed the coaching staff throughout the offseason, earning high praise from Clanton as “the best center in the world.” He took advantage of the spring practices while Dominic Rulli was out with an injury, continuing to put on weight and take first-team reps.

Penn State’s interior is experienced and primed to come together for a great first season playing together for the Nittany Lions.

Kicker

The kicker is an underappreciated position group in football as it stands, often only noticed when mistakes are made or when games come down to the wire. However, the kicker is also the most reliable way to score points, and pairing a consistent leg with a strong defense could be Penn State’s way of slowly chipping away at opponents.

In an offensive system that doesn’t know where it stands among the Big Ten, Ryan Barker’s influence may be the safety net the Nittany Lions need.

Barker established himself as one of college football’s premier kickers last season when he broke Penn State’s single-season record for field goal percentage with 94.7%. As an incoming redshirt junior, he’s made 33 total field goals and is 92-for-94 on extra point attempts.

Close games are often decided by the final drive, and Barker isn’t a stranger to clutch situations. In his redshirt freshman season, Barker scored Penn State’s first first game-winning field goal since 2014, a 36-yard strike to beat USC on the road in overtime.

title: The newest additions to Penn State women’s hockey’s incoming class
author: Dominic Megats I The Daily Collegian
description:
In his ninth season as head coach, Jeff Kampersal took the Penn State women’s hockey program to a new level: The Frozen Four.

Though they lost eight core seniors after the season concluded, for the Nittany Lions, gain often follows loss. Kampersal welcomed ten newcomers to his squad this offseason, three of which being transfer players. Six forwards, two defenseman and two goalies are featured in the new class.

Take a look at the new players set to wear the blue and white.

Transfers

Ashley Kokavec, defenseman

Kokavec, a 5-foot-5 defenseman, transferred once before making her way to Happy Valley as she spent her freshman season at Maine before spending her next two at Vermont.

The Palm Beach, Florida, native is coming off a season where she led all defenseman in points at Vermont with 17. Kokavec finished tied for third among Hockey East defensemen in assists with 14.

Alanna Devlin, forward

The second transfer addition comes from Boston College. Devlin played her first two collegiate years as an Eagle. There, she tallied 18 total points in 59 games.

Before committing to Boston College, she played 220 total games for North America Hockey Academy totalling 200 points and served as captain in her senior season.

Savanna Muir, goalie

Muir makes her way to Penn State after spending two seasons with SUNY Cortland. Although she didn’t see any time in net for the team, the Elizabeth, Pennsylvania, native found production with the Bishop Kearney Selects, where she recorded six shutouts in 11 appearances, finishing with a 9-1 record as a starter.

Recruits

Kylie Amelkovich, forward

One of the more promising forward recruits coming to Happy Valley is Amelkovich. The Glenn Illyn, Illinois, native spent three seasons at St. Mary’s Prep before committing to Penn State. There, she scored 76 goals in 152 games, totalling 159 points. Additionally, she represented Team USA in the 2025 and 2026 IIHF U18 Women’s World Championship.

Sofia Ismael, forward

Another emerging young forward makes her way from up north. Ismael played three seasons with the Etobicoke Dolphins along with representing Team Canada at the IIHF U18 Women’s World Championship in both 2025 and 2026.

With the Dolphins, Ismael recorded 171 points in 125 games. She captured gold with Canada in 2025 after posting four points in six games.

Megan Hosman, defenseman

The only defenseman in the freshman class makes her way from The Loomis Chaffee School along with spending some time with the Mid Fairfield Stars. Hosman donned the “C” as she captained her team through her senior year at Loomis Chaffee.

She earned the New England Defender of the Year award for the second-straight season after recording 29 points in 28 games.

Kayla McCarthy, forward

McCarthy, a Pennsylvania native, spent six seasons with the Pittsburgh Penguins Elite. In her final season, she recorded 20 goals and 21 assists, finishing with 41 points in 57 games.

She qualified for the USA Hockey National Championship five times.

Sydney McIntosh, forward

The Langley, British Columbia, native is coming off a season with RINK Hockey Academy Kelowna where she recorded 39 points in 48 games.

McIntosh helped her team capture the 2026 CSSHL Championship title before making her way to Penn State. She tallied seven points in five games in the playoffs.

Lorelai Nelson, forward

Nelson joins the Nittany Lions after four impressive seasons at Edina High School. She posted 179 points in 151 games, netting 82 goals.

The Edina, Minnesota, native served as captain in her final season and became a finalist for the 2026 Ms. Hockey Award. In addition to that award, Nelson earned All-Conference honors throughout her four years in high school and earned All-State honors twice. She finished her time at Edina High School averaging 1.12 points per game.

Morgan Stickney, goalie

Stickney is the sole netminder recruit in the young class. Starting in 34 games, the Manhattan Beach, California, native earned a 1.28 goals against average and a .944 save percentage.

Her final stat line at St. Mary’s earned her a spot on Team USA at the IIHF U18 World Championship for the second-straight year. She went 2-0-0 with two shutouts.

title: Council president says borough ‘close’ to Addison Court purchase as redevelopment talks continue
author: Jonathon Chiu | The Daily Collegian
description:
State College Borough Council President Evan Myers began Monday’s meeting announcing the borough was close to an agreement to purchase Addison Court from PrimeCore Properties, an effort to maintain its affordability for senior residents and residents with disabilities in downtown State College.

As negotiations are ongoing, Myers didn’t provide details; but he said any agreement produced from talks would be discussed in a public meeting as part of a regular council agenda.

The council also voted unanimously to schedule a public hearing for Sept. 9 to resume discussions of PrimeCore's request for a height limitation amendment to the 200 block of South Allen Street located next to Addison Court. The borough will provide an amendment draft to the Centre County Planning & Community Development office and the Centre Regional Planning Commission for comment prior to the public hearing.

PrimeCore, which took over ownership of Addison Court from Beaver Court Associates in May, plans to demolish the building for a mixed-use structure called Encore.

While PrimeCore CEO Ara Kervandjian said a preservation plan for Addison Court is currently being explored, construction of Encore would commence if attempts to restore the building’s status within the Low Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) program were unsuccessful.

Addison Court’s status within the LIHTC, meant to maintain affordability for its tenants, expired on Dec. 31, 2024.

Kervandjian previously indicated that PrimeCore would still pursue construction of Encore should the amendment request be rejected.

The height limitations, set by borough ordinance 1597, are 65 feet. According to rationale for the amendment, part of the council’s April 20 agenda, PrimeCore argued the limitations prevent Encore from matching the appearance of Pugh Centre next door, another PrimeCore apartment development. It said this prevents it from pursuing its original plan of a “uniform 7-story 72-foot-high building.”

The planning commission voted 3-2 during its June 18 meeting to recommend the council reject the request.

title: Key Penn State position battles heading into fall camp
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State will roll out a starting lineup that looks a lot different from last year, including Rocco Becht at quarterback, Carson Hansen at running back and more.

While many positions are already set for this year, there’s a number of starting spots that are still up for grabs.

Here’s a look at some position battles heading into fall camp.

Backup quarterback

Last season at Iowa State, Becht was the starting quarterback while Alex Manske held the backup spot. That duo remains, but this time at Penn State.

Unlike last year, Manske has competition for the second-string role, as the Nittany Lions brought in senior Connor Barry from Christopher Newport. With Manske recovering from an undisclosed injury and Becht rehabbing a torn labrum, Barry took a majority of starting snaps during spring ball.

The senior quarterback led the Captains to an undefeated regular season while becoming a semifinalist for the Gagliardi Trophy, which is awarded to the best Division III player, and a Second Team All-American.

However, Matt Campbell believes deeply in Manske. He said at Big Ten Media Days in Chicago that Manske has been cleared to participate in fall camp, elevating the backup quarterback battle once again.

Manske has very little collegiate experience, while Barry took a majority of first-team reps throughout the spring. If Manske can make enough of an impact over the next month, he may slot in as backup. However, Barry’s experience over the last six months gives him the slight edge heading into fall practice.

Defensive end

While young returnees Max Granville and Yvan Kemajou were both looking to start this season, Penn State’s defensive end room grew in depth during the offseason.

Campbell brought in veteran Ike Ezeogu from Iowa State and sophomore Alex McPherson from Colorado, both of whom are expected to battle for a starting spot.

Two starting jobs appear available, with all four expected to factor into the rotation. Granville will have to make a quick impact this fall after being out for almost an entire year with an undisclosed injury, while Kemajou showcased a bit of what he’s capable of toward the end of 2025.

Campbell talked about Granville’s recovery and the buzz around him returning to full health for fall camp in Chicago. Meanwhile, Anthony Donkoh praised both Granville and Kemajou for their strength and potential this season.

Left tackle

Penn State’s offensive line has just one returning starter in Donkoh at right tackle. While Trevor Buhr, Brock Riker and Cooper Cousins are expected to fill in the rest of the line, the left tackle spot is still up for competition.

Additionally, Campbell spoke with Jeff Byers on his radio show about the left tackle being a position to watch this season.

Redshirt freshman Malachi Goodman has received praise from the new staff and was the starting left tackle during the spring. At 6-foot-6, 320 pounds, the former 4-star commit has the physical traits to succeed on Ryan Clanton’s offensive line.

However, redshirt sophomore Garrett Sexton is another competitor for the role after backing up Nolan Rucci last season and filling in as the starting right tackle this spring with Donkoh sidelined. Sexton appeared in 13 games in 2025, including playing left tackle early in the year.

Also throwing his name in the hat is redshirt freshman Owen Aliciene. All three linemen were praised by Campbell throughout the spring, saying “I don't know if I could be any more impressed with what I've seen from that group.”

Defensive tackle

Unlike the defensive ends, Penn State’s defensive tackles boast numerous veterans who are competing for a starting role.

Among the older players are Keanu Williams and Siale Taupaki, who have a combined 11 years of collegiate experience. However, redshirt sophomore Armstrong Nnodim has shined during the spring and made a name for himself among the coaching staff.

Williams will likely earn a starting role after making 23 starts over the past three years with UCLA. However, the other role will likely be between Nnodim and Taupaki, as Penn State will utilize a four-down front, per Campbell in Chicago.

Nnodim has the recent momentum after starting four games last year and earning praise during the spring, but Taupaki has veteran experience and has seen the starting lineup in recent years.

title: Off the record | The double standard of sex
author: Miss Behave I The Daily Collegian
description:
Editor’s Note: Off the record is a weekly column written by a fourth-year Collegian staffer under an alias. It aims to promote a space for honest conversations about love, sex and relationships. Those interested in sharing their experiences or submitting a topic can do so through this anonymous form.

Dear reader,

Episode 3 of Alex Cooper’s Call Her Daddy podcast has the following description: “The ultimate blow job technique that is guaranteed to be every man's kryptonite. Introducing- The Gluck Gluck 3000.”

Maybe you read the words “blow job” and were instantly thrown back to your own experience. Or maybe your body physically tensed up, not having had the topic on your roster for today: How dare I talk about, let alone open a column with, something so promiscuous?

I get it, we’ve been trained to think of anything sexual as off the table for conversation or not ladylike. But I’m not subscribing to that anymore.

Cooper, alongside other media personalities, is teaching women that talking and engaging in sex is normal, the same way it is for men. I’m sure everyone reading this can recall having to listen to a man go on and on about his latest hook-up, but can you recall doing the same?

The early days of Call Her Daddy were driven by stories about sexual encounters, mistakes and subsequent lessons her audience could learn from. Today, she conducts more formal, sit-down interviews. I can only assume the backlash she received has contributed to her new episode style, but we need the very sex talk that made Cooper famous now more than ever.

We all do it, so why is it some secret people don’t dare speak about? College, especially, is a time when people are exploring and learning, and it extends outside the classroom. I’m not saying we should be reckless in the pursuit of sex, but let’s not ignore the facts. 65% of students at Penn State are sexually active, according to a Collegian survey from February, and why shouldn’t they be? It’s a college town full of young adults who — newsflash — have sex. I’m so tired of pretending we need to tiptoe around the topic.

Do you whisper about sex? Like whispering to your friend about your other friend’s weird attitude; to your therapist about a bad thing you did last week.

I’m sure you’ve thought of it as a secret, a dirty one at that. I’m sure you’ve felt the general social pressure to pull the topic back in your throat and only let it depart from your tongue in a private space, accompanied by your closest confidants.

Well, do you whisper about how good your favorite song is? What about your favorite restaurant? I bet the answer is no.

By containing all of the same qualities as a dirty secret, sex has all the subsequent, negative associations, too. That chain reaction of something shameful:

It ends up reserved, and reserved things aren’t for public display, so reserved becomes private.

Privacy implies there’s something to hide, and hiding something implies the thing-in-hiding is bad.

I actually don’t think that society as a whole has a problem talking about sex. In fact, I think a rise in sharing personal stories on social media (and on podcasts, of course) has normalized it more, albeit only slightly. Still, when women do it, problems arise. Misogyny runs rampant. They’re subjected to every name in the book, labeled a whore, a slut, not-the-marrying-type.

I implore you to think about what a label actually does. It takes a contextualized, deeply human thing, and puts it in a box. “This is a nighttime activity.” “This is a bedroom activity.” “This is a married-people activity,” or a shameful one, or a sacred one.

But I don’t think humans find sex innately private nor shameful. We don’t come out of the womb feeling these ways about sex, yet in our society, having sex is perceived as more vulnerable than being seen crying, or being seen fail, or being seen at your worst in hundreds of other non-sexual ways.

Being overly crude is one thing when it’s uninvited, and we can definitely cross a line. Casual conversations about sex, though, aren’t hurting anyone, and they provide a space for genuine questions everyone’s probably wondering. We all had to learn from somewhere. There’s no point in being confused and left in the dark when the answers are out there, you just have to be brave enough to ask.

When it’s uncomfortable to talk to loved ones about something as intimate as sex, having spaces where people can be as unfiltered as they want proves to be a guiding light. If we don’t provide answers to women, they’ll inevitably seek them out elsewhere.

The spread of misinformation regarding sex can be extremely dangerous and easily prevented with open dialogue with women who aren’t going to be silenced just to please the social standards set before them.

Maybe the people who read this column will vehemently disagree, because it makes them uncomfortable to hear about other people's sexual experiences, or merely read the word sex. In a way, that’s exactly my point. Put on your big girl pants, grow up and stop forcing other people to act a certain way just to make you feel better. Sex isn’t a bad word.

Until next time,

Miss Behave

title: Penn State OL Anthony Donkoh’s off-field leadership shows strong correlation to new coaching staff
author: Andrew Deal | The Daily Collegian
description:
Anthony Donkoh announced he’d return to Penn State on Dec. 30, just three days after the Nittany Lions’ Pinstripe Bowl victory over Clemson.

Now, Donkoh has emerged as a leader on the team, joining teammates Rocco Becht and Tony Rojas as Penn State’s player representatives at Big Ten Media Days, and has led by example both in the offensive line room and among the team, which has to come together in a short time for the 2026 season.

“Anthony was actually the first young man that decided to come back to Penn State when we got to campus,” Matt Campbell said at Big Ten Media Days. “Anthony's a young man whose work ethic, his character, has truly led us both on and off the football field.”

Donkoh's experience as a two-year starter and versatility allows him to better become a leader both on and off the field. While his on-field play has done a lot of talking in the past, it’s clear the redshirt junior has taken on a leadership role off the field as well, stating “it wasn’t hard” to bring the players together as one team.

Campbell’s philosophies early on have quickly aligned with how Donkoh approaches things, especially when it comes to team chemistry. The Virginia, native had a strong 2025 season, but he’s consistently remained humble in his game, something that Campbell has preached to every player through the first six months.

“If you're a humble person, people always gravitate to you easily, and that's how you walk into the room, and that's why I like him a lot as a person,” Donkoh told reporters in Chicago.

While Penn State has yet to step onto the football field in this new era, the team has been growing together as one unit. Donkoh took an approach to build bonds and connections early on in the calendar year to already have a better connection on the field even during spring practices.

“It’s better that we built the bonds fast off the field than before when we get on the field because on the field stuff can be superficial, but off the field stuff, like you're my brother, that's how it has to be, and that's how it has been. So that's been great,” Donkoh said.

With a large group of Penn State’s team coming from transfers from all over the country, Donkoh believes getting to know his teammates and growing together off the field will help the play on the field when the Nittany Lions begin their first season under Campbell in the fall.

“When you do things off the field and you guys are able to bond really well, that immediately translates to the field because you guys are building the trust and faith in those people before you even step on the field,” Donkoh said. “So, like, if something goes wrong, this is how he acts. I know how he is, and so we can be able to move forward from that, and be able to still have that same trust and faith.”

title: ‘You got to be in love with the process’ | How Matt Campbell’s philosophy has impacted Penn State
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
Shortly after Matt Campbell became head coach at Penn State, two new signs were installed in the Lasch Building meeting room. One had four paragraphs about culture, with words like team, excellence and respect in bold, while the other listed the “Nittany Lion Code of Conduct,” encouraging saying thank you, you’re welcome and addressing people as sir and ma’am.

Over six months later, players say those principles have become some of the most noticeable changes within the program.

“Coach Campbell takes (accountability) to a whole other step,” Anthony Donkoh told reporters at Big Ten Media Days in Chicago. “This helps us build a lot of leadership, which we need to be successful on the field.”

As part of fostering leadership, Campbell created accountability groups throughout the roster. When players make mistakes on or off the field, teammates are expected to help each other learn and grow from them.

One of Campbell’s biggest messages has been that no one is above learning. Even as one of Penn State’s veteran leaders, Tony Rojas said he’s continued to lean on teammates for guidance while rehabbing from a torn ACL.

Rojas specifically said he’s had help from the leaders from Iowa State like linebacker Kooper Ebel and safety Marcus Neal Jr.

That willingness to learn extends beyond the players, with the coaching staff also molding to the team’s strengths and weaknesses and adapting its schemes to fit its personnel rather than forcing players into a rigid system.

Rojas said previous defensive coordinators often “called plays the coach wanted rather than what us players are best at.”

“I’ve had multiple different coordinators every year, so this year it’s finally where I could learn different types of defense-like schemes every year,” Rojas said. “It’s pretty easy, and coach Lynn has done a great job.”

As the Nittany Lions work toward Week 1, the players’ focus has been on team success. While several guys are projected to have breakout seasons that could improve their NFL draft stock, individual accolades have taken a back seat.

“Everybody knows that this is bigger than themselves,” Donkoh said. “At the end of the day, we need to kill our pride and be humble about things and how we move around ourselves. If you're humble, people can gravitate towards you and be able to share anything with you, and that makes sure that everybody's tight together and wants to fight for a cause.”

A big proponent of humble football is Campbell, who Donkoh described as a very modest guy. Despite making the move to a major Big Ten program Penn State, Campbell is only focused on making his team better.

As Campbell enters his first season leading the Nittany Lions, the team’s attention has stayed on the process rather than outside expectations.

“The difference I feel is this year we’re trusting the process more,” Donkoh said. “Just focus on what you can do every day to make a difference, because you got to be in love with the process. (Campbell) brings great energy and cares about your development. He’s a great coach, and I’m excited for this season.”

title: Staff predictions | Which corporation should partner with Penn State for a jersey patch?
author: The Daily Collegian Football Staff
description:
The jersey-patch era is upon college football.

Notre Dame and Ohio State announced record-breaking deals this week with SoFi and Chase Bank, respectively. The Fighting Irish are receiving somewhere from $18 to $20 million annually to sport the SoFi logo, while the Buckeyes are earning $17 million each year.

Penn State will potentially follow suit soon, as Vice President for Intercollegiate Athletics Pat Kraft told reporters in Chicago at Big Ten Media Days that the Nittany Lions are open to exploring jersey patches.

Here’s which corporations we think could ink a jersey-patch deal with Penn State in the future.

Andrew Deal: First National Bank

Penn State added a trio of stripes on July 1 with the transition to Adidas, and what better way to go all in on the “three stripe life” than with some more stripes, but this time of First National Bank’s logo.

While the Nittany Lions may not receive the sum of money that the Buckeyes or Fighting Irish are from a banking company, it could still get a large amount from a company like First National Bank.

First National Bank in particular makes sense for multiple reasons. The university announced in March its partnership with the bank, establishing it as the university’s long-term retail banking and financial services provider.

On the other hand, the logo for First National Bank features both of Penn State’s colors, blue and white. Although it has a bit of red in it — a color that’s pretty universally frowned upon at Penn State — it’s only a tiny part of the logo and can make the patch pop on the uniforms.

Other brands could make even more sense, given even closer connections to Penn State, but with First National Bank, it could garner the biggest annual payment, adding more in the pot to thrive in the new era of college football.

Andrew Mercer: Utz

When walking through the aisles of grocery stores nationwide, it’s hard not to notice the Little Utz Girl with her dark blue hair and bright red bow.

Utz would be a strong match for a jersey patch, considering Penn State’s particular emphasis on fan engagement. Spectators adore the tailgating culture of football games among other experiences where chips, pretzels and other snacks are staples of the culture. Seeing more of the Utz logo wouldn’t be out of the ordinary.

It’s a household name, particularly in the Keystone State, as the company hails from Hanover, Pennsylvania. As snacks are a common item at parties and cookouts, and the brand has a wide variety of flavors and textures, there isn’t an issue of recognition.

Utz was named the Official Potato Chip Partner of Penn State Athletics in 2018, so there’s already a concrete business link between the pair. The company also has a history of sponsoring the local professional sports teams as well, notably including the Philadelphia Phillies, Eagles and the Pittsburgh Pirates.

A simple logo of three bold letters and the iconic mascot would fit nicely on the jerseys, and it wouldn’t be so striking that it’d take away from the plain uniforms Penn State is known for.

Lexie Linderman: Hershey

Arguably the most well-known corporation in Pennsylvania is The Hershey Company, not to mention the fact that it’s one of the biggest chocolate brands in the entire world. It just makes sense to have the premier business in the state supporting the premier college athletic department.

If Penn State wants the most lucrative deal it can get, Hershey might be its best bet, considering the scope of the company. And the Nittany Lions should go after a big sum. They’re a top-10 brand in college football, so it’s only right they find a corporation that will pay them as such.

The city of Hershey is just about two hours from Penn State, so the regional ties are very much there. The Nittany Lions are also present in the community, as the football team visits Penn State Health Golisano Children's Hospital in Hershey annually.

As for how the logo would look on Penn State’s basic blues, it would look pretty clean. Hershey’s emblem is very simple, with just the company name spelled out in silver capital letters. Switch that to blue and white and it’ll blend in nicely on the home and away uniforms.

A deal with Hershey also embodies Penn State by playing into its in-state roots and the family feeling the athletic department tries to create with fans.

Noah Aberegg: Sheetz

There’s been a long-running battle between Sheetz and Wawa for the title of Pennsylvania’s favorite convenience store. What better way for Sheetz to settle that debate than by becoming a premier sponsor for one of the nation’s most recognizable college football programs?

After placing its logo on the Pittsburgh Pirates’ uniforms, Sheetz has shown it sees value in prominent sports partnerships. Adding Penn State to that portfolio would further strengthen its identity as Pennsylvania’s top gas station.

The deal may not rival the financial value of partnerships with major banks or financial technology companies, but it could resonate with Penn State’s fan base in a way few sponsors can. Sheetz has become a staple across much of Pennsylvania, making it a natural fit for the Nittany Lions.

While Sheetz’ red-and-yellow branding differs from Penn State’s traditional color palette, the logo would create a striking contrast against the Nittany Lions’ navy or white uniforms without overwhelming their classic look.

As Wawa is extending into Central Pennsylvania, a partnership with Penn State would reinforce Sheetz’s roots in the Commonwealth State while giving the Nittany Lions a sponsor that feels authentically connected to their fan base. It’s a win-win for both sides.

title: 10 classic things Penn State seniors should do before graduating
author: Justin Elliott | The Daily Collegian
description:
If you ask any Penn State graduate about their years on campus, they’ll almost certainly tell you that the four undergraduate years fly by in the blink of an eye.

Many alumni leave State College having fulfilled everything on their bucket list, while some don’t even realize they missed out on some iconic traditions until it’s too late. But don’t worry, you do have time to do it all.

Here’s 10 things Penn State seniors should check off their list before graduating.

Attending LightsUP and Movin’ On

What better way to open and close the school year than huge concerts?

LightsUP is Penn State’s student-run opening concert that’s been held on the HUB lawn at the end of August each year since 2021. Movin’ On, one of the largest student-run music festivals in the country, is the counterpart of LightsUP and an iconic send-off event held in May each year.

It’s been around for 51 years, previously featuring headliners like Sexyy Red, JID, Dayglow and, most recently, Zara Larsson.

Getting a Berkey Creamery sweet treat

An on-campus favorite, the Berkey Creamery is essential to both Penn State’s history and students’ sudden cravings for a sweet treat. The signature ice cream shop has been around for over 150 years and features flavors ranging from “Death by Chocolate” to “Peachy Paterno.”

It’s open seven days a week — much to the delight of students all over the town.

HUB lawn sledding

The borough saw absurd amounts of snowfall last winter, with the highest single-day accumulation reaching over 12 inches in January.

Though State College snow can make your fingers numb, it also provides the optimal conditions for sledding down the HUB-Robeson Center’s massive lawn. There, students can be seen taking advantage of canceled classes by sledding, throwing snowballs or making snow angels every winter.

Bar crawling

While there are only a select number of opportunities to sled on campus, there’s many more chances to participate in bar crawls throughout the school year.

Bar crawls are organized and often themed public events where participants visit a list of bars or pubs in one day, usually receiving discounts, t-shirts or costumes. Some of the most popular ones in State College are the Back to School, Santa, State Patty’s and Summer Send-Off crawls.

Hiking Mount Nittany

If you’re more into nature than bars, climbing the vast, scenic landmark known as Mount Nittany is a must. The well-preserved mountain of nearly 1,000 acres consists of over eight miles of trails for students, alumni and the simply adventurous to traverse in their free time. Whether you’re more of a casual hiker or want to test your endurance, Mount Nittany is a sight to behold.

Visiting The State Theatre

Those that are fans of the arts or avid cinephiles should visit the State Theatre at least once. The performing arts center has been in town since 1938, offering a selection of movies, musicals, live broadcasts and more at an affordable price every week throughout the year.

Keep an eye on the theatre’s weekly announcements and you’re likely to catch a classic showing.

Seeing a show at the Bryce Jordan Center

The Bryce Jordan center is a multi-purpose arena that’s not only home to the school’s Division I basketball teams, but often the venue that sees the biggest names in music and entertainment every year.

With a capacity of over 15,000 people, it’s the largest of its kind in the region, hosting names like Drake, Billie Eilish, Kane Brown and other artists as well as comedians and fine arts performers over the years. Don’t miss out on seeing arena-level stars at student-rated discounts right on campus.

Of course, going to a White Out Game

While every football game at Penn State is bound to be one of the more electric experiences one can get at the school, the annual “White Out” game is undoubtedly the most highly anticipated one each year.

Whether you’re at the game — which often attracts crowds of over 100,000 people — at the tailgates, or downtown, the energy in State College on the day of White Out is one every student should feel before graduating.

Arts Fest-ing

Unless you’re taking a summer class, you may not see much reason to visit State College in the summer. If you’re into the arts, however, you might want to consider returning in July.

Every summer, the Central Pennsylvania Festival of the Arts comes to town, and a resurgence of over 100,000 visitors with it. From paintings to performances, hundreds of artists bring original work, tucked into tents or lining the streets.

THON

The Penn State Dance Marathon, better known as THON, is perhaps the most uniting event of the year in State College for students.

Over 16,000 student volunteers participate in nonstop dancing and activities for 46 hours straight, fundraising millions of dollars each year to fight childhood cancer. The Bryce Jordan Center comes alive with student organizations, long lines, food and live music as the community unites “For The Kids.”

Whether you’re participating or supporting, THON is a one-of-a-kind event for students to attend before graduating.

title: What to know as Mount Nittany workers enter fourth day of strike
author: Grace Levy | The Daily Collegian
description:
On Monday, union employees represented by SEIU Healthcare Pennsylvania began a planned five-day strike at Mount Nittany Medical Center.

Here’s what to know as the strike enters its fourth day.

How many people are on strike?

According to SEIU Healthcare Pennsylvania, 950 workers — nurses and staff members represented by the union — are on strike.

But members of other local unions have also joined the picket line in support of the Mount Nittany workers, including members of the teachers, steelworkers, bricklayers, electrical and teamsters unions.

Why are they striking?

In a Facebook post, SEIU Healthcare Pennsylvania said its top priorities are “fair wages that recruit and retain experienced workers for community care as well as improvements in workplace and patient safety.”

“They have been struggling to support their families with the spiraling costs of living in Centre County, and Mount Nittany executives have not even offered raises that cover inflation,” the post read.

Fawn Guignet, an ER nurse and member of the union’s bargaining committee, has worked at Mount Nittany for over 10 years. She said she worked as a monitor clerk before finishing nursing school last year, which helped her understand the importance of having support staff.

“They don't feel that we deserve even a living wage, let alone enough to meet inflation. That's the big thing,” Guignet said. “They need to still be able to afford to work here and to be part of our patient care team.”

SEIU Healthcare Pennsylvania’s post also said Mount Nittany is the fourth most profitable hospital in the state with over 30% profit margins, and “has more than enough resources to reach an agreement that invests in all employees responsible for providing renowned care.”

“The majority of people who work here don't even live in Centre County just because the cost of living in this part of the state is so expensive. The cost of living is comparable to that of Pittsburgh,” Jenna Cowan, a medical laboratory scientist and union chapter vice president, said. “They haven’t given us a wage increase to match the cost of inflation.”

The average cost of purchasing a home in Centre County has nearly doubled since 2017, a disparity more pronounced in regions closest to State College, according to the Centre Daily Times.

Unionized employees and Mount Nittany Medical Center executives have been in the negotiating process for a new labor contract since April 29. The last contract expired June 30, and union members voted in favor of a strike on July 2.

During a July 21 negotiation meeting, Mount Nittany offered a one-year contract extension; three percent across-the-board wage increase for all union members; $1,000 ratification bonus for every bargaining unit employee; wage scale upgrades for 18 job classifications; and continued investments in workplace safety in their most recent proposal, according to the Mount Nittany Health website.

The union rejected this offer, saying it is not a fair increase, WPSU reported.

How long will the strike last?

The strike will continue until Saturday at 7 a.m. Contract negotiations are expected to resume after the strike.

“We're just ready to get back inside. We want to get a contract,” Josh Rosefsky, an utility specialist in maintenance and member of the union’s negotiating committee, said. “We're ready to negotiate as soon as they get the authority to actually move on their wages, because that's the big thing, where they keep getting told that they don't have the authority to move on anything.”

Rosefsky said the negotiations are for all employees, rather than just one individual department.

“The hospital tried to split us up. They wanted better raises for nurses and not everybody else. Our entire membership, they didn’t want that,” Rosefsky said. “This hospital does not run just on nurses. It is environmental services. It is respiratory. It is the kitchen. It’s lab, imaging, it's ED nurses, it’s regular nurses.”

Are patients affected by the strike?

People with scheduled appointments, procedures and treatments should plan to attend unless contacted directly by a member of their care team, according to Mount Nittany’s website.

The emergency department will remain open.

Select outpatient labs and imaging locations will have temporary changes to their hours during the duration of the strike.

Mount Nittany Health Lab - PhilipsburgMount Nittany Health Lab - Blue Course DriveMount Nittany Health Lab - Hospital Drive

Select locations will be closed throughout the strike. This includes:

Mount Nittany Health Lab - Penns ValleyMount Nittany Health Lab - BellefonteMount Nittany Medical Center - Outpatient LabMount Nittany Health Imaging - Penns Valley

title: Penn State Women's volleyball's Kennedy Martin Named to AVCA Player of the Year Watchlist
author: Rafael Rivera | For the Collegian
description:
Kennedy Martin has been nominated to the AVCA Player of the Year Preseason Watch List, the association announced Wednesday.

Martin earned a spot on the list for the third time in her collegiate career. The 6-foot-6 right-side hitter from Fort Mill, South Carolina, will her senior year as one of the top players in the country with a hefty resume, including All-SEC honors in 2023 and 2024 with the Florida Gators and First-Team All-Big Ten in her first season with Penn State.

She matched that total with another 34 kill performance against Ohio State on Nov. 16, helping Penn State achieve a 3-2 reverse sweep.

Martin will serve as one of the Nittany Lions’ most dangerous offensive weapons coming into 2026, and will be poised to have an impactful senior campaign.

title: ‘I just can't wait’ | Penn State QB Rocco Becht, now fully healthy, is eager to get back on the field
author: Andrew Mercer | The Daily Collegian
description:
When Rocco Becht arrived on campus, he was limited in his throwing reps due to lingering injuries to both of his shoulders. While he used the time to curate personal connections with his new teammates, he lost out on live reps this spring.

But now, Becht is itching to go. The winningest quarterback returning to college football revealed at Big Ten Media Days in Chicago that he’s fully healthy and expressed his gratitude for everyone who helped him through the process as well.

“Recovery's going great,” Becht told reporters in Chicago. “The training staff and the waiver staff have done a great job with me. Not just me, but everyone on our team that's been injured. But yeah, I'm super anxious for college football to be back, really fall camp because I wasn't able to do a lot in spring. But I just can't wait to go back out there.”

Campbell took the time to speak about Becht’s character while he was up on the podium at Big Ten Media Days, telling the audience that he’s earned everything he’s accomplished, with his grit, character and toughness leading the way.

Becht has already shown those traits in his few months as a Nittany Lion. While he couldn’t make an impact on the field this spring, he chose to establish himself as a leader in the locker room, helping forge bonds between former Cyclones and the Penn State returnees.

“I think to win games to succeed in college football, you got to have those bonds. You can't just have relationships with me as you know a quarterback to a quarterback, quarterback to a receiver,” Becht said. “I got to have relationships with everyone. The D line, the corners, the linebackers, and that's something that I've been able to work on.”

Throughout the spring and summer, Campbell brought back a series of Penn State lettermen to speak with the team. Becht got to learn from past star Nittany Lion gunslingers such as Todd Blackledge, Trace McSorley, Christian Hackenberg and Kerry Collins about the unique position he’s entered — the pressures, expectations and realities of being a Penn State quarterback.

“Being able to speak to those guys about how to be a Penn State quarterback is something that I've been able to instill in myself over the past summer,” Becht said. “Hopefully being able to go out there and play like a Penn State quarterback this season.”

Even his nickname, “Mr. President,” allegedly coined by wide receiver Chase Sowell, is something that he doesn’t let go to his head, although Becht thinks it’s “pretty funny.”

With Becht, Sowell, Brett Eskildsen, Koby Howard and the rest of the offense now fully healthy, Penn State has no limitations on that side of the ball, and Becht is optimistic about where the Nittany Lions can go from here.

“​​The chemistry is there,” Becht said. “Fall camp is kind of just that exclamation point of putting everything together before the season.”
